summary: The Ed25519 signature algorithm has been implemented in OpenSSH. This document updates the IANA registry of SSHFP public key algorithms by adding an algorithm number for Ed25519, so SSH host keys of that type can be published in DNS.

eli5.summary: SSH servers have keys, and DNS can list fingerprints for them. This adds the newer key type to the list of kinds that DNS understands.

questions: how to publish ssh ed25519 fingerprint in dns
what is the ed25519 sshfp algorithm number
how to publish an ed25519 ssh fingerprint in dns
subtitle: Gives Ed25519 SSH host keys a number in the SSHFP DNS record so their fingerprints can be published.

tldr.problem: OpenSSH had implemented the Ed25519 signature algorithm, but the SSHFP DNS record had no algorithm number for Ed25519 keys.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 7479 adds value 4, Ed25519, to the IANA registry of SSHFP public key algorithms and shows an example record using a SHA-256 fingerprint.
tldr.outcome: Administrators can publish fingerprints of Ed25519 SSH server keys in DNS in the same way as for other key types.

today: RFC 7479 is an Informational document, and no later RFC is listed as obsoleting or updating it.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
The Ed25519 signature algorithm, specifically Ed25519-SHA-512, has been implemented in OpenSSH. RFC 4255 defines a DNS resource record called SSHFP, which publishes a fingerprint of an SSH server public key in the DNS.

This document updates the IANA registry of SSHFP public key algorithms by adding an algorithm number for Ed25519.
sections.eli5: SSH servers have secret-handshake keys, and DNS can list a short ID for each one. A new kind of key just needed its own place on that list.

sections.title: Ed25519 Key with a SHA-256 Fingerprint
sections.content:
An Ed25519 public key is a 32-octet value representing a 255-bit y-coordinate of an elliptic curve point, plus a sign bit for the corresponding x-coordinate. The encoding is described in the Ed25519 paper.

The RFC gives an example SSHFP record for ssh.example.com with algorithm 4, fingerprint type 2 (SHA-256) and a hexadecimal fingerprint. The opaque octet string produced from the public key file body is placed as is in the RDATA fingerprint field.
sections.eli5: You take the key, squash it into a short fingerprint, and write that fingerprint into DNS as is.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The overall security of using SSHFP for SSH host key verification depends on the security policies of the SSH host administrator and DNS zone administrator, on how verification is done in the SSH implementation, and on the client's diligence in accessing the DNS in a secure manner.

The RFC refers readers to RFC 4255 for the full discussion.
sections.eli5: A fingerprint list is only as trustworthy as the people who fill it in and the way you look it up.

sections.title: The IANA Registry Entry
sections.content: IANA added one entry to the SSHFP RR Types for public key algorithms registry: value 4, description Ed25519, reference RFC 7479.
sections.eli5: The official list of key types got a new line: number 4 is Ed25519.

references.text: Schlyter, J. and W. Griffin, "Using DNS to Securely Publish Secure Shell (SSH) Key Fingerprints", RFC 4255, January 2006.
Bernstein, D. J., Lange T., Schwabe P., and B-Y. Yang, "High-Speed High-Security Signatures", Journal of Cryptographic Engineering, Vol. 2, September 26, 2011.
